newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Aug 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The latest threat to the Bangkok Asian Games appears to have been averted when the Olympic Committee of Asia appealed to Santiparb Tejavanija, the event's marketing chief, to reconsider his resignation. Sheikh Ahmad al-Sabah al-Fahd, president of the OCA, has told Santiparb that his continued efforts are crucial to the success of the 1998 Games. (BANGKOK POST)

- A decision by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to support the passage of the draft constitution would probably boost his party's popularity at the next general election, which would be held under the new charter, social critic Theerayuth Bunmee says. He says a vote of approval from Chavalit's New Aspiration Party is essential for the passage of the draft charter through Parliament. (THE NATION)

- Italian-Thai Development Plc may be given a chance to take over from Hopewell (Thailand) Co, which is struggling to fund its delayed mass transit project. Last year, Ital-Thai sought a majority stake in Hopewell but failed to convince Gordon Wu, head of Hopewell Holdings, to accept its conditions. (BANGKOK POST)

- The team of economists and financial experts from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will finalise its rescue package for the Thai economy this weekend, and Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya will submit the proposal to the Cabinet for approval next Tuesday. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has indicated his approval in principle of the effort to obtain IMF assistance. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Amazing Thailand must generate 700 billion baht or the country will be in trouble, the prime minister says. Thailand is pinning its hopes on the 1998-99 promotion, says Chavalit, who also calls on people to save money and be frugal. (BANGKOK POST)
